title: Compact standby handoff cheatsheet (scratch)
content:
Purpose: quick, portable notes for a compact weekend standby handoff. Not a formal runbook — this is my personal crib for covering overlapping releases + capacity noise. Use as crib to send Slack handoff, update TG when needed, and flag follow-ups.

Context / current state:
- Friday evening: two small releases gated (release window: 18:00–22:00 PT). Primary risk: embedding pipeline CPU spike + transient quota errors on hosted API.
- Dedicated: scheduled autoscaler test tomorrow at 03:00 UTC — may cause temporary pod churn.
- Observability: tracing retention reduced for weekend, but we still have token-level traces for flagged routes.

Quick top-line for whoever is picking up:
- Primary objective: keep the customer-facing API within latency SLOs and avoid noisy paging. Let the release run unless deterministic 5xx spike > 2% sustained for 5m.
- Secondary objective: protect Dedicated commitments — abort autoscaler test if scale events cause >3m elevated tail latency on reserved pools.

Slack handoff template (paste + tailor):
"Hey team — Lucien handing off standby to @<NAME>. Active items: 2 small releases (RELEASE-337, PR #1948) finishing deploy; scheduled autoscaler test at 03:00 UTC. Watch hosted-api route /v1/generate for 5xx or 99th percentile latency > 2.0s. If anything looks off, DM me and escalate to @Aisha and @Rowan. Pager policy as usual (pager channel #infra-pager). I'm reachable via phone if needed. — Lucien"

Monitoring quick check (first 10 mins):
- Check SLO dashboard: hosted-api 99p latency, error-rate (scope: route /v1/generate).
- Alerts to scan: HOSTED-ERROR-RATE, DEDICATED-TAIL-LATENCY, KV-CACHE-MISS-ALERT.
- Dashboards: console/route/hosted-api (bookmark), infra/autoscaler (bookmark).
- Logs: search for surge patterns "rate_limit_exceeded", "kv_cache_miss=1".

Immediate triage decision tree (short):
- If 5xx rate spikes above 2% sustained for 5m: 1) Identify if spike correlates to a single route/model. 2) If route/model = newly deployed release → roll back (PR #1948 rollback script: /scripts/rollback_release.sh) and notify release owner. 3) If generic backend errors (DB/connectivity) → page SRE.
- If 99p latency > 2.5s for hosted-api: 1) Check batching-queue depth; 2) Check KV cache hit rate; 3) If KV cache miss > 30% and coincides with elevated latency, enable warmed prefixes (console quick toggle) or increase cache capacity for the short window.
- If Dedicated tail latency spikes > 3x baseline during autoscaler test: abort autoscaler test (see steps below) and revert scaler policy.

Autoscaler test abort (fast steps):
1) Go to infra/autoscaler > active policies > test-policy-RELEASE-337.
2) Pause policy (button), confirm any pending scale actions are canceled.
3) If pods are mid-rotation, open support ticket to ops (CON-4821) and trigger governance rollback for the cluster.

Escalation contacts (order):
- Oncall SRE: Aisha Gomez (primary) — Slack @aisha, mobile +1-XXX-555-0143.
- Platform lead: Rowan Patel — Slack @rowan, mobile +1-XXX-555-0122.
- Release owner: Priyanka Shen — linked PR owner for #1948.

Short checklist to leave at handoff (tick these in Slack message):
- [ ] Confirm deploys finished (no pending pods).
- [ ] Confirm autoscaler test scheduled start time and owner.
- [ ] Confirm logging retention toggles for weekend.
- [ ] Push a short note into #infra-shift about who is stepping in.

Common gotchas + shorthand notes (notes-to-self):
- If you see immediately rising token billing spikes: likely noisy evals hitting hosted API. Check usage -> api/keys -> top callers and hit-rate. Consider temporary token-level throttling for offending keys (console: throttle quick action).
- Debugging high embedding latency: often caused by small-batch loop in client side; check request shape (embedding.size field). If top callers are internal test harnesses, throttle at source.
- KV cache warmup: rapid deployments can invalidate hot prefixes. Use cache-warm script: tools/warm_cache.sh with prefix list from /ops/weekly-hot-prefixes.csv.

Draft internal Q&A snippets (for cross-team Slack thread or quick all-hands blurb):
Q: Will the autoscaler test affect customer traffic?
A: It can if scaling events coincide with heavy tail loads; we have an abort flow and will pause test if we see degraded tail latency. Customers should not see sustained errors — we'll keep the page if risk passes thresholds.

Q: Are there any planned rollbacks tonight?
A: No rollbacks planned proactively. If the release shows regressions (error-rate > threshold), we will rollback and communicate in #release-updates.

Q: How to reach you?
A: Slack DM is fastest. If I don’t respond in 10m and the impact is customer-visible, page SRE and call me.

Follow-ups to file after incident (put in a ticket for Monday):
- Confirm whether the autoscaler test needs a different guardrail (add 10% delay between scale events).
- Look into adding a lightweight synthetic for hosted-api route /v1/generate to catch regressions before customers see them.
- Add a quick rollback runbook to the release PR template.

Unresolved questions / TODOs (my personal scratch):
- Is there a short-term setting to reduce tracing verbosity for weekends without losing token-level traces? (ask Observability team).
- Confirm phone numbers for escalation list (update metadata).

End notes (personal):
- Keep the handoff short. The goal is to avoid waking folks for noise. If the problem is ambiguous, err on the side of calling the release owner first before broad paging.
- When you hand back in the morning, drop a 1-paragraph summary into #infra-shift and tag the release owner + oncall.

Raw commands I often use (stash):
- Quick error snapshot: curl -s "https://console/api/metrics?query=error_rate[5m]&route=/v1/generate" | jq .
- Rollback (safest): /scripts/rollback_release.sh RELEASE-337 --confirm

-- end of scratch crib --

Notes: keep this private; it's a working scratchpad for next-person handoff wording. Will formalize into a runbook if this pattern repeats.
